action.action-desc: Mr. Levin of Michigan (for himself and Ms. Stefanik) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Education and Labor

form.official-title: To establish a task force on supplemental foods delivery in the special supplemental nutrition program, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the COVID–19 WIC Safety and Modernization Act.

section.header: Task force on supplemental foods delivery in the special supplemental nutrition program

subsection.text: Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this section, the Secretary shall establish a task force on supplemental foods delivery in the special supplemental nutrition program (in this section referred to as the Task Force).

paragraph.text: The Task Force shall be composed of at least 1 member but not more than 3 members appointed by the Secretary from each of the following:

subparagraph.text: Technology companies with experience maintaining the special supplemental nutrition program information systems and technology, including management information systems or electronic benefit transfer services.
Participants in the special supplemental nutrition program from diverse locations.
Other organizations that have experience with and knowledge of the special supplemental nutrition program.

paragraph.text: The Task Force shall be composed of not more than 20 members.

The Task Force shall study measures to streamline the redemption of supplemental foods benefits that promote convenience, safety, and equitable access to supplemental foods, including infant formula, for participants in the special supplemental nutrition program, including—

subparagraph.text: online and telephonic ordering and curbside pickup of, and payment for, supplemental foods;
online and telephonic purchasing of supplemental foods;
self checkout for purchases of supplemental foods; and
other measures that limit or eliminate consumer presence in a physical store.

paragraph.text: Not later than September 30, 2021, the Task Force shall submit to the Secretary a report that includes—

subparagraph.text: the results of the study required under paragraph (1); and
recommendations with respect to such results.

paragraph.text: Not later than 45 days after receiving the report required under paragraph (2), the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.text: submit to Congress a report that includes—

clause.text: a plan with respect to carrying out the recommendations received by the Secretary in such report under paragraph (2); and
an assessment of whether legislative changes are necessary to carry out such plan; and

subparagraph.text: notify the Task Force of the submission of the report required under subparagraph (A).

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall make publicly available on the website of the Department of Agriculture—

subparagraph.text: the report received by the Secretary under paragraph (2); and
the report submitted by the Secretary under paragraph (3)(A).

subsection.text: The Task Force shall terminate on the date the Secretary submits the report required under paragraph (3)(A).
The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall not apply to the Task Force.

paragraph.text: The term local agency has the meaning given the term in section 17(b) of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 (42 U.S.C. 1786(b)).
The term Secretary means the Secretary of Agriculture.
The term special supplemental nutrition program means the special supplemental nutrition program under section 17 of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 (42 U.S.C. 1786).
The term State agency has the meaning given the term in section 17(b) of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 (42 U.S.C. 1786(b)).
The term supplemental foods has the meaning given the term in section 17(b) of the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 (42 U.S.C. 1786(b)).
